behavior.drop: dropping an accepted CONNECT result publishes one atomic removal request for its fixed slot without allocating a Job, taking the endpoint mutex or occupying the command queue
behavior.capacity: at most one pending generation per fixed Session slot; requests coalesce and one endpoint pending flag avoids scanning slots on ordinary turns without cleanup work
behavior.generation: live generation publication precedes result delivery; retirement clears it before resource release; pending is acquired before checking live generation so an old request cannot replace a newer generation request
behavior.owner: after claiming a command, process cleanup before execution, including cleanup published while claim was waiting on the mutex; recheck the cleanup flag after wake reset to retain a concurrent request
behavior.lifetime: the accepted result retains State through its request publication; owner shutdown retires fixed slots, so retained accepted results remain safe to drop after the endpoint owner is destroyed

regressions: duplicate removal requests coalesce; the valid new generation replaces an already pending stale request; subsequent stale requests cannot overwrite it

drop an accepted result while endpoint mutex is held and command queue is full, with both available and denied caller allocations; require zero allocation attempts and no mutex wait, unchanged queue links/count and no new Job reference
the real owner processes cleanup published while claim was blocked before executing the existing command; occupied failed Session marker is removed and its generation advances
retain an accepted result across endpoint owner destruction, then drop it with caller allocation disabled without touching freed State

real authenticated TLS multiplexed-Session case drops a genuine accepted result under the endpoint mutex with caller allocations denied; cleanup stays pending without another queue entry and subsequent traffic proceeds

independent Python peer accepts a CONNECT that is dropped, requires RST_STREAM(CANCEL), then receives a new CONNECT on the same connection; native max_sessions=1 client requires the same slot with a new generation and exchanges exact DATAGRAM and CLOSE
verification.fault_boundary: allocation denial is restricted to the dropping caller; these tests prove cleanup publication cannot fail from caller Job allocation or mutex admission, and do not assert behavior of arbitrary allocator failures in later wire output

remaining_scope: server admission/cleanup surfaces, broad protocol integration and multi-hour/high-concurrency evidence remain open for the full library goal
